keys: en:Imagine a README that says: install the dependencies, start the development server, and open the local address printed in the terminal. These steps must be completed in order. The document also says that the sample data is stored in the project. You do not need an account to use it. However, saving your changes requires permission to write to the project folder.
en:First, check your Node.js version. Then install the dependencies and start the development server. Finally, open the local address in your browser.
en:Before starting the server, check your Node.js version.

en:A useful bug report describes what you expected and what actually happened. For example: I expected the search results to update after I changed the filter. Instead, the page showed the old results. A clear comparison helps another developer understand the problem before they open the code.

en:Next, give the shortest steps that reproduce the problem. Include the browser version and the exact error message, if there is one. Do not guess the cause without evidence. A teammate might find a cause you did not expect. After a fix, repeat the same steps to check the result. A screenshot can help, but it does not replace a clear description.
en:I expected the search results to update when I changed the filter. Instead, I still saw the old results. I can reproduce it by changing the filter twice.
en:I expected the page to update. Instead, it showed the old data.

en:Learning a skill is different from memorising a list of facts. When you learn to cook, for example, you need to understand instructions and then try them. The first attempt may fail, but it shows you which part needs attention. Small, regular practice sessions can be easier to maintain than an ambitious schedule that you soon abandon.

en:Feedback also matters. A teacher can point out a mistake, but the learner still has to practise the new approach. Recording yourself can be useful because you notice things you miss while speaking. You might hear a long pause or find that an example is unclear. The aim is not to remove every mistake at once. It is to choose one useful change and test it in your next attempt.
en:I study computer science. I enjoy practical courses because I can turn an idea into something useful. For example, I recently built a website with two classmates.
